headline: Germany's Profligacy Proves Costly Against Pragmatic Ecuador
story: Germany made the perfect start with an early goal but Ecuador showed character, equalizing just minutes later in a way that suggested they understood the task. What followed was a match of contrasts: Germany monopolized possession—51 per cent to 39—yet seemed frustratingly unable to convert their control into concrete advantage. Ecuador's lower possession masked a disciplined structure and willingness to strike on transition. The turning point came when their clinical finishing, particularly an incisive 77th-minute strike, finally broke German resistance.

Germany's problem was simple: quantity over quality. They forced more turnovers (51 versus 49) and recovered possession faster, yet generated lower expected goals (0.74 to Ecuador's 1.29). Leroy Sané, Florian Wirtz and Jamal Musiala animated the midfield, but Nilson Angulo and John Yeboah's defensiveness blunted their threat. Ecuador's higher xG despite possessing just 39 per cent reflects ruthless finishing. At 77 minutes, when Ecuador struck decisively, the match tilted irreversibly: Germany had pressed relentlessly but couldn't convert. Their dominance had been illusory.

keyMoment.text: Ecuador strikes decisively; Germany's relentless pressing finally fails to deliver.

home.verdict: Clinical finishing and defensive discipline overcame German possession dominance.
points: Higher expected goals (1.29 vs 0.74) converted ruthlessly through decisive attacking.
Absorbed possession deficit with organized defending; Angulo (7.7) and Yeboah (7.2) proved immovable.
Survived two blocked or missed big chances (73', 77') then capitalized—efficiency when it mattered.

away.verdict: Early goal squandered; late inefficiency proved fatal against clinical opponents.
points: Quick 2' lead demolished by 9' equalizer; momentum never recovered in opening flurry.
Expected goals deficit (0.74 vs 1.29) despite 11 shots exposed poor chance positioning.
Sané, Wirtz (7.5, 7.4) dominated but lacked penetration; Ecuador's 77' riposte trumped 76' saved shot.

statLine: Ecuador's 1.29 expected goals with half of Germany's possession revealed this was about precision, not volume.
